Quran-Nazm · hizb layout study

10 pages per hizb, four shrink limits

The first page of hizb 14, which opens in Al-Anʿām at ayah 36 and ends on ayah 44. Each hizb is first set as one unstretched Digital Khatt line, cut into 10 pages at ayah ends (all nine cuts chosen together so the pages hold equal amounts of text), and each page is cut into 15 equal lines at word boundaries, with no line starting on an ayah marker. All four sheets are the same physical size.

The problem to hide

Hizbs are not the same size

Set at Madina type size with no stretching, the 60 hizbs would fill anywhere from 8.5 to 11.6 pages. Giving every hizb exactly 10 pages means this spread has to be absorbed by stretching the short hizbs and shrinking the long ones.

Hizbs 1–58Juz 30 (hizbs 59–60), handled as an exception

The shortest is hizb 42 (8.53 pages) and the longest is hizb 50 (11.55 pages), a ratio of 1.35. Half of all hizbs fall between 9.4 and 10.6 pages; the standard deviation is 7.7% of the mean. Lengths are text only: surah headers add further lines to the hizbs where surahs begin, which is why hizb 55 rather than hizb 50 sets the line width in the layouts below.

Variation in line stretch inside a page is 0.039 at every shrink limit, against 0.065 in the Madina 1441H print (standard deviation of log stretch). The shrink limit changes the type size and where the stretch is centred, not how even the lines are.

Extremes at 25% shrink

The densest and the sparsest page

Hizb 55 (from Al-Mujādila) is the densest hizb, with lines averaging 0.94× across all its pages; hizb 15 (Al-Anʿām) is the sparsest at 1.31×. Below is the most compressed page of the first and the most stretched page of the second, at the same line width and type size as the 25% render above.

The compressed page shows the limit of a 25% budget. Tightening spaces and the font's narrow forms recover only part of the width, so every line on it is also squeezed horizontally, by up to 19%, which visibly narrows the letters. Across the Mushaf, 51% of compressed lines need some horizontal squeeze at this limit, and 24% need more than 5%. The stretched page has no such distortion, only long elongations.

Shrink limits from 10% to 45%

What each shrink limit buys and costs

All rows use the same layout of hizbs 1–58; only the common line width changes. "Squeezed" counts lines where tightening spaces and the font's narrow forms are not enough and the letters themselves are scaled horizontally.

For reference, the Madina 1441H print compresses 16% of its lines by more than 10% (up to 27%), always through the calligrapher's own letterforms, never by squeezing letters. Line evenness inside a page is the same at every limit.

Method: text from the 1441H layout data, set in the QMH New Madina font, juz 30 excluded. Madina-style surah headers take two lines (one for Al-Tawba) on the page where the surah begins. The common line width is set by the longest line produced anywhere in hizbs 1–58, narrowed by the shrink limit. Lines were justified with the Digital Khatt letter-stretching rules ported in quran-madina-html v2; shrinking tightens spaces and uses the font's narrow forms before any horizontal scaling. Page frames and line spacing are schematic.
